mechanics.name: Deception
mechanics.currentEffect: While running, interact with a Locker to fake entering it: you run past instead, the Locker door opens and closes, and a Loud Noise notification is created at that Locker. Your Scratch Marks and Pools of Blood are suppressed for 5 seconds. Cooldown: 25/20/15 seconds.
activation: Be running near a Locker and use the interaction input.
Ends/deactivates when: Scratch Mark and Pool of Blood suppression ends after 5 seconds.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.6.0): Reduced the cooldown to 25/20/15 seconds.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: A fake Locker entry creates a decoy noise while briefly hiding your trail.
duration: Scratch Marks and Pools of Blood suppressed for 5 seconds.
specialInteractions: The fake Locker interaction creates a Loud Noise notification at the Locker.

editorial.summary: Fake a fast Locker entry while running, create a noise notification there, and hide Scratch Marks and Blood for 5 seconds.
useCases: Break line of sight near a Locker and sell the fake entry.
Use the 5-second trail suppression to continue past the Locker without leaving the expected path.
Pair repeated 15-second cooldown mindgames with Locker-oriented builds.
counters: Experienced Killers can ignore obvious fake Locker attempts.
Direct sight, Aura reading, and sound can reveal the continued route.
The trick is weaker when the map has no useful nearby Locker.
pros: Combines false information with trail suppression.
Can create real chase mistakes against a conditioned Killer.
cons: No direct distance or health-state protection.
analysis: Deception ranks this position because its modern 15-second cooldown and five-second trail suppression make it more than a comedy perk. The Locker notification presents one story while hidden Scratch Marks and Blood allow the Survivor to tell another.

The perk gets stronger over multiple encounters. Once a Killer has seen you use Deception, they may start second-guessing real Locker entries as well, especially in builds that also contain Head On or Quick & Quiet.

The skill is selling the fake. Triggering Deception in full view accomplishes little. Breaking line of sight first and choosing a Locker positioned near multiple possible routes is what converts the perk into chase value.
It stays in B because it never guarantees a mistake. Strong Killers can keep visual contact or simply refuse to check the Locker. Deception rewards creativity, not certainty.
editorial.verdict: A genuinely useful misdirection perk in practiced hands. Deception creates false information, but the Survivor still has to make the lie believable.
